children.counts: Basic 1-2-3-4 counts to match the primary xylophone.
children.game_version: A 'follow the leader' game where children mimic the warrior steps of the elders.

seniors.counts: Simple 4/4 pulse instead of complex polyrhythms.
seniors.seated_version: Perform the rhythmic arm movements and shield placements while seated; focus on the m'zeno singing.
seniors.standing_version: Slow-tempo warrior steps with the support of a spear used as a staff.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced to the slow m'zeno tempo; avoid fast rhythmic shifts.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Carrying and maneuvering shields, spears, and head-breakers.
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic 'warrior steps' (pas de danses guerriers) that respond to the xylophone strikes.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Linear or small group formation (2-12 people) positioned in front of the seated orchestra.
movement_profile.partnering: None; individual movements within a group formation.
movement_profile.posture: Martial and upright; ready for combat-inspired movements.

signature_moves.description: Martial footwork inspired by 19th-century Zulu conflicts.
signature_moves.name: Warrior Step

signature_moves.description: Slow, solemn movement performed while singing satirical lyrics.
signature_moves.name: M'zeno Song Accompaniment

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Alternates between slow, solemn movements and high-tempo rhythmic sections.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid generic 'folk' movements; the dance must maintain its specific martial and historical character.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Independent rhythms for left and right hands; 9-10 movement structure (ngodo)
music_profile.sound_description: A rich, buzzing nasal sound produced by wooden slats over calabash resonators. The music is characterized by dense polyrhythms where the orchestra creates a wall of sound with varying pitches and registers.
music_profile.tempo_bpm: Varying (alternating between slow m'zeno and fast orchestral sets)
music_profile.vocal_style: Call-and-response; solemn, humorous, and sarcastic lyrics

basic_steps: Warrior stance with shield and spear held ready
Rhythmic footwork synchronized with the lead xylophone (chilanzane)
Coordinated shield strikes or spear thrusts on specific counts
Slow, solemn walking during the m'zeno song section
teaching.formation: Two to twelve dancers in a line or group in front of the orchestra.
teaching.level_notes: Requires high rhythmic coordination to match the varying tempi of the ngodo sets.
teaching.rhythm: Complex polyrhythms; left and right hands of musicians play different patterns.
